title: Daytona process-session bind for vault stdio MCP
description:
Follow-on from lp-oop.38.17.

stdio MCP that must see /mnt/vault cannot run as toolbox process/execute (JSON-RPC session, not one argv). v1 fail-closes honestly.

When a tenant needs vault MCP, bind a long-lived Daytona process session (or put an HTTP MCP in front of the vault). Do not fake it with execute.

Acceptance:
- Documented session API (create/attach/RPC/teardown) or an HTTP MCP that sees the mount
- use_tool on a vault-required stdio server uses that session, not process/execute
- Guest create-env still has no MCP secrets
notes:
Playbook: feature.md. architect skipped: two shapes (A Daytona process-session JSON-RPC create/attach/exec/input/logs/teardown vs B guest HTTP MCP sidecar + preview URL). Picked A — bead names the session API, Daytona already has stdin/logs (spike-4dk), no extra snapshot binary, no Fargate-to-guest preview. Throughput: blocking=session types + path guard vs process/execute; independent=CP HTTP client vs create-env MCP denylist vs LA use_tool bind; shared state=one session per (sandbox_id, server) via vaultMcpSessionId attach; smallest decomp=ToolboxProcessSessionClient + bindVaultMcpStdioSession. Principles: model-the-domain (session port vs execute port), foundational-thinking (JSON-RPC session before invoke), laziness (no sidecar), redesign (vault_session is a real bind not a fail-closed bolt-on), boundary (parse at HTTP/config edge), type-system (discriminated session ops), separate-before-serializing (session map keyed by server, FakeToolbox execute isolated), build-the-lever (fake session + bind tests), prove-it-works (shared 7, CP 12, LA 14+19).
Platform PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/560 (990689b1). LA PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-agent/pull/257 (2edad3f). Tests: shared session 7, CP session+create-env 12, invariants+bind 10, LA mcp+session+runner 33.
Fix pass: live catalog mcp_count=0 has_vault_stdio=false was the root cause (session client unused). Seed vault_fs into BACKEND_HOME + fill-missing /mnt/vault/mcp/vault_fs_server.py. Platform 2fe7a3b2 PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/560. LA 9223dab PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-agent/pull/257. Tests: merge 8, seed smoke PASS, shared 7, CP 12, LA 34.
Fix pass: merge vault_fs before tools factory (createEnvToolsTurnRunner captures BACKEND_HOME) and continue JSON-RPC ids on reattach. Platform ae26e571 PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/560. Tests: shared 7, CP 12, merge 8, seed/short-stack/replace-echo smokes PASS. architect skipped: already recorded on parent notes (A process-session vs B HTTP sidecar; picked A).
Fix pass: local echo was the root cause (use_tool never ran). Kitchen-sink FakeHarnessHttp now binds bindVaultMcpStdioSession on vault-MCP chats (tool pills, command column, not echo; execute=0). Start wrapper runner=tools-lab when LiteLLM is missing. LA snapshot includes command. Platform d88121d1 PR 560. LA f6c7762 PR 257. Tests: shared vault-fs-turn 4 + session 7 + fake-http 12; CP 12; merge 8; replace-echo smoke PASS (tools-lab); LA snapshot+mcp+runner 54 + schema 118 + settings 17. Live catalog still empty until image roll. needs_ui_qa=true (kitchen-sink, no HARNESS_URL).
Implementer re-verify (worktree /tmp/lp-bead-lp-oop.38.19): HEAD d88121d1 already on origin; PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/560 draft (no second PR, no new commit). Playbook feature.md. architect skipped: already recorded (A Daytona process-session JSON-RPC vs B guest HTTP sidecar; picked A). Principles: model-the-domain (ToolboxProcessSessionClient vs ToolboxClient.execute), foundational-thinking (JSON-RPC session types before invoke), laziness (no sidecar), redesign (vault_session is a real bind), boundary (parse at HTTP/config edge), type-system (discriminated session ops), separate-before-serializing (session map keyed by server, FakeToolbox execute isolated), build-the-lever (fake session + bind tests + merge-vault-fs-mcp.mjs), prove-it-works (shared 23, CP 12, merge 8, replace-echo PASS, short-stack harness PASS). Acceptance met offline: documented session API; kitchen-sink use_tool binds process/session not process/execute; guest create-env strips MCP-named keys. Companion LA https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-agent/pull/257. Live catalog still empty until harness image roll. needs_ui_qa=true (kitchen-sink FakeHarnessHttp, no HARNESS_URL).
close_reason: Merged: platform #560, LA #257 (via #256). ToolboxProcessSessionClient JSON-RPC session, not process/execute. vault_fs seed + merge-vault-fs-mcp. Guest create-env still strips MCP keys.

title: Show each agent's cron jobs and wake the sandbox when one is due
description:
## Why
Users need the list of cron jobs for that agent, and a due job has to wake the computer. The registry and evaluator already exist (`scheduled-job-registry.ts`, `schedule-evaluator.ts`). Settings already has a list. This bead binds that list to the Cloudflare alarm and the Daytona wake.

Plan: `docs/plans/0020-cloudflare-platform-revamp/overview.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The portal lists jobs for the selected agent from the durable registry
- [ ] Creating a short-interval job persists across a control-plane restart
- [ ] When the alarm fires, ensure_online runs and the job execution is recorded
- [ ] A second agent's list does not include the first agent's jobs
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Per-agent list from the durable registry
- [ ] Due job wakes the sandbox and records the run

title: Wake a Daytona sandbox from Workers and attach the R2 filesystem
description:
## Why
The computer is a Daytona sandbox. It persists, goes idle, and wakes when the agent needs it. The control plane orchestrator already models ensure_online, idle grace, and a durable vault prefix. Point that orchestrator at the Workers control plane and an R2 prefix.

Plan: `docs/plans/0020-cloudflare-platform-revamp/overview.md`. One sandbox while proving this. Plan 0008 identity rules stay: instance_id permanent, sandbox_id ephemeral, prefix durable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A stopped sandbox starts when a chat turn or the cron alarm needs it
- [ ] The R2 prefix is mounted or otherwise visible as the agent filesystem after wake
- [ ] Idle stop still runs after the grace period
- [ ] A file written before stop is present after the next wake
- [ ] Spend notes record sandbox count and that platform-staging was not re-enabled
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Wake on chat or cron, then idle stop
- [ ] R2 files survive that cycle

title: Serve BFF, control plane, and the portal from Workers
description:
## Why
Fargate and CloudFront were the always-on AWS cost. The localhost loop should answer from Workers once D1, R2, Durable Objects, and the API-key backend path exist.

Plan: `docs/plans/0020-cloudflare-platform-revamp/overview.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A workers.dev (or local wrangler dev) host serves the SPA
- [ ] BFF routes used by the localhost chat turn run on that host
- [ ] Control plane is not a public route; BFF reaches it by service binding or the local equivalent
- [ ] The same chat turn as the localhost bead succeeds against this host using base URL + API key
- [ ] Platform-staging AWS is not applied
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] SPA and BFF answer on Workers
- [ ] Control plane is not public
- [ ] Chat turn matches the localhost proof

title: Add a Cloudflare API token for Workers, D1, R2, and Durable Objects
description:
## Why
Local D1, R2, and Durable Object work uses wrangler locally. Deploying the portal needs a real account. The operator offered to add Cloudflare permissions.

Plan: `docs/plans/0020-cloudflare-platform-revamp/overview.md`.

## Token
Account ID plus an API token with Workers Scripts Edit, D1 Edit, R2 Edit, and Durable Objects Edit. Store it as a local secret (`chmod 600`), never in git. Daytona and model keys stay separate secrets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] wrangler whoami succeeds with that token
- [ ] The token is not committed
- [ ] Notes name the account id and which products the token can edit, without the token value
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] wrangler whoami succeeds
- [ ] Token is not in git
notes: Human gate. Local database and filesystem beads do not wait on this.

title: Replace Valkey sessions, leases, and cron alarms with Durable Objects
description:
## Why
ElastiCache Valkey held BFF sessions, relay JTI replay keys, presence, and leases. The schedule evaluator also needs an always-on clock so cron can fire while the sandbox is stopped. Durable Objects cover both the coordination and the alarm.

Plan: `docs/plans/0020-cloudflare-platform-revamp/overview.md`. This is not a WebSocket relay.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A local Durable Object stores a BFF session and expires it
- [ ] A second responsibility records sandbox presence and a singleflight wake lease
- [ ] An alarm API accepts a next_run_at and invokes the existing schedule-evaluator entry when it is due
- [ ] Tests use the workers runtime locally, not Redis
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Session, presence lease, and cron alarm work locally without Redis

title: Store the agent filesystem on R2
description:
## Why
The agent's files outlive the sandbox. Today that is an S3 prefix mounted into the guest. Mountpoint first-write is slow (`lp-puzc`) and the bucket is an AWS cost. R2 is the S3-compatible replacement.

Plan: `docs/plans/0020-cloudflare-platform-revamp/overview.md`. Identity stays `instance_id` permanent, vault prefix durable, `sandbox_id` ephemeral (plan 0008).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A local R2 (wrangler or Miniflare) bucket stores tenants/{{tenant}}/agents/{{agent}}/vault/
- [ ] Writing a file and restarting the process still returns the same bytes
- [ ] The control plane is the only writer of credentials for that bucket
- [ ] A note records whether the Daytona guest can mount the same prefix with an S3-compatible endpoint
- [ ] No AWS bucket is created
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Vault bytes survive process restart on local R2
- [ ] Prefix layout is per agent
- [ ] Mount note for the guest is recorded

title: Accept the Cloudflare service map before any Workers code
description:
## Decision
Replace the torn-down AWS platform with Cloudflare, and keep Daytona as the agent computer.

- `portal_cp` and Prisma `portal_app` move to two D1 databases. Control-plane SQL in `portal/packages/control-plane/src/migrate.ts` is the port. Do not keep RDS behind Hyperdrive.
- Valkey sessions, JTI, presence, leases, and cron alarms move to Durable Objects.
- Vault files, artifacts, and chat corpus move to R2. The guest may mount R2 with an S3-compatible client.
- BFF and control plane move to Workers. The control plane is reached by service binding, not a public route. The SPA is Workers static assets.
- DNS, TLS, and WAF move to Cloudflare.
- Platform secrets are Worker secrets. Per-tenant model keys are encrypted in D1. Local password sessions stay valid without Cognito.
- Chat does not gain a new Durable Object relay in v1. The connection is the base URL + API key from the backend bead.
- EC2 company-brain, VPC, account factory, and cross-account IAM are not migrated.
- ONLYOFFICE stays local Docker for this epic.

## Rationale
The AWS bill and the OPERATOR HOLD are why the project paused. D1, R2, Durable Objects, and Workers cover the services that were actually running the portal. Daytona already owns idle and wake, which Cloudflare Containers would only reimplement. Hyperdrive would keep the Postgres cost.

## Alternatives Considered
- Hyperdrive to RDS: keeps the database being removed.
- Cloudflare Containers as the agent computer: conflicts with the Daytona sandbox the product already models.
- Durable Object relay as the primary chat bus: repeats the Valkey relay that the harness path is replacing.
- Big-bang portal UI rewrite: chat, vault, settings, cron, and office UI already exist.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] This decision matches `docs/plans/0020-cloudflare-platform-revamp/overview.md`
- [ ] Amendments, if any, are written on this bead before D1, R2, Durable Object, or Workers implementation starts
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Decision matches the plan overview
- [ ] Amendments land here before cloud implementation
notes: The map is proposed by the plan. Close this bead when a human accepts it or after amending the plan in the same change.

title: Move control-plane and product tables onto local D1
description:
## Why
Two Postgres databases back the portal: `portal_cp` (tenants, users, roles, gateway instances, scheduled jobs, connectors) and `portal_app` (Prisma businesses, folders, OAuth tokens, model provider tokens). Both need a Cloudflare home before Workers can boot without RDS.

Plan: `docs/plans/0020-cloudflare-platform-revamp/overview.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Wrangler local D1 has a portal_cp database whose tables cover the localhost loop (tenant, user, instance, scheduled job)
- [ ] A second D1 database holds the portal_app tables the loop touches (business, user, model provider token)
- [ ] Existing control-plane migrate SQL is the source for portal_cp; Postgres-only types (enums, uuid, text arrays) have an explicit SQLite form
- [ ] A test boots the control plane against local D1 and reads a tenant row
- [ ] Hyperdrive and RDS connection strings are not required for that test
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Local D1 serves portal_cp and portal_app tables for the loop
- [ ] Control plane test reads a tenant with no Postgres

title: Connect an agent backend with a base URL and an API key
description:
## Why
Chat currently forks between Relay WSS (`CHAT_DELIVERY=relay`) and harness HTTP, and model calls still expect LiteLLM plus an AWS Secrets Manager envelope. Lanyard Agent drops `brain_rpc_request` (external issues 134–137). A localhost agent should be any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or a Lanyard harness, addressed by base URL and API key.

Plan: `docs/plans/0020-cloudflare-platform-revamp/overview.md`. Keep the harness HTTP turn from plan 0015. Do not add a second relay.

## Shape
`base_url`, `api_key`, `protocol` (`openai_chat` or `lanyard_harness`). One model is enough. Composer tier routing (ADR 0007) stays optional.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Localhost chat completes with those three fields and no relay process required
- [ ] No Cognito and no Secrets Manager call on that path
- [ ] A bad API key fails with a visible error and does not fall through to Hermes defaults
- [ ] Hermes-specific settings reads go through the existing backend runtime contract
- [ ] Tests cover both protocols with a fake server
design: Protocol openai_chat posts to the configured chat completions URL. Protocol lanyard_harness posts the existing turn request to HARNESS_URL-shaped base_url with the API key as a bearer token. Relay remains in tree for old guests and is not the default for this loop.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Chat uses base URL + API key only
- [ ] Bad key fails visibly
- [ ] Fake-server tests cover both protocols
notes:
Localhost chat uses three fields and does not need a relay process.

Env: AGENT_BACKEND_BASE_URL, AGENT_BACKEND_API_KEY, AGENT_BACKEND_PROTOCOL (openai_chat | lanyard_harness). Optional AGENT_BACKEND_MODEL (default "default"). The API key is Authorization: Bearer. openai_chat POSTs that URL as chat completions. lanyard_harness POSTs {base}/internal/turns and reads message_send from the event stream.

Proof 2026-10-15: relay stopped (8787 down). BFF started with AGENT_BACKEND_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4310, AGENT_BACKEND_API_KEY=placeholder-harness-service-token, AGENT_BACKEND_PROTOCOL=lanyard_harness. Curl history returned assistant "Echo harness: hello via api key". Browser chat returned "Echo harness: office check" once. Process chat_delivery stays relay; the send path returns before relay thaw, and history/SSE skip relay when the backend is set.

Bad key: fake-server tests return 401 "invalid api key" / "unauthorized" with one request and no Hermes reply. Hermes settings: resolveAgentBackendSettings calls BackendRuntimeService.snapshot when a runtime is injected, otherwise the offline fixture. agent-backend.ts does not import Hermes discovery, Cognito, or Secrets Manager.

Tests: portal/packages/bff/test/agent-backend.test.ts (8 passing).
close_reason: Localhost chat completed with base URL, API key, and lanyard_harness while relay was stopped. Fake-server tests cover openai_chat and lanyard_harness, including a rejected key.

title: Boot the current portal on localhost and record the agent loop
description:
## Why
The restart has to begin from a running system. `portal/docker-compose.yml` is already the local stack (Postgres `portal_cp` + `portal_app`, BFF :4000, Relay :8787, control plane on 127.0.0.1:3100). AWS staging must stay down.

Plan: `docs/plans/0020-cloudflare-platform-revamp/overview.md`.

## What to prove
Use the fake backend or the local harness. Do not point this boot at torn-down staging hosts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Postgres, BFF, relay, and control plane health checks pass on localhost
- [ ] One signed-in chat turn returns an assistant message
- [ ] The scheduled-task list for that agent renders, including the empty state
- [ ] A vault file reads back through the local provider or Brain RPC
- [ ] Notes name the exact commands, the chat path used (relay or harness), and anything that failed
- [ ] No terraform apply and no ECS desired-count change
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Local health checks pass
- [ ] One chat turn completes
- [ ] Scheduled-task list renders
- [ ] A vault file reads back
- [ ] Notes record commands and the chat path
notes:
Booted 2026-10-15 on native Postgres (docker unavailable). No terraform apply and no ECS desired-count change.

Commands:
- Postgres: postgres://portal:portal@127.0.0.1:5432/portal_cp and portal_app (role portal). Health: PGPASSWORD=portal psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U portal -d portal_cp -c 'select 1'
- Built missing workspace dist so BFF could import them: pnpm --filter @lanyard/hermes-compat --filter @lanyard/connectors --filter @lanyard/backend-runtime --filter @lanyard/chat-corpus run build
- Echo harness: node deploy/dev/localhost-echo-harness/serve.mjs (127.0.0.1:4310, token placeholder-harness-service-token)
- Control plane: CONTROL_PLANE_DATABASE_URL=postgres://portal:portal@127.0.0.1:5432/portal_cp CONTROL_PLANE_SERVICE_TOKEN=placeholder-control-plane-service-token pnpm -C portal dev:control-plane
- Seed: CONTROL_PLANE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3100 CONTROL_PLANE_SERVICE_TOKEN=placeholder-control-plane-service-token portal/scripts/seed-demo-tenant.sh then portal/scripts/assign-demo-member-roles.sh (run again after the google stub user exists)
- Relay: source portal/.data/demo-env.sh && pnpm -C portal dev:relay
- BFF: source demo-env.sh, plus CONTROL_PLANE_DATABASE_URL (same URL), HARNESS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4310, HARNESS_SERVICE_TOKEN=placeholder-harness-service-token, VAULT_ROOT=/tmp/lanyard-localhost-vault (file notes/boot.md), CHAT_STORE_PATH=portal/.data/chat.db. CHAT_DELIVERY left unset. pnpm -C portal dev:bff
- Web: source demo-env.sh && pnpm -C portal dev:web (http://127.0.0.1:3010)

Health: control-plane :3100, relay :8787, bff :4000, echo harness :4310, postgres select 1. All ok.

Chat path: harness (localhost echo). HARNESS_URL selects the spine/harness hop. Process chat_delivery stays relay. Relay is up for the health check and is not the chat hop. pnpm dev:mock-gateway cannot run; portal/scripts/dev-mock-gateway.ts was removed and dev-tmux.sh still launches it.

Proof: signed in as dev@demo.local in the browser. One chat turn returned assistant text "Echo harness: ping from browser" once. Scheduled-task list rendered the fixture jobs "Settings snapshot export" and "Vault index refresh" (empty state was not the path; the list rendered). Vault file /notes/boot.md read back "localhost boot note" through the filesystem provider.

Failures: a curl events client for an earlier turn saw the same turn_id streamed three times (spine remember is called three times; same-owner claim can re-enter). Filed lp-bhcg.19. The browser showed one bubble. Google stub user had no member role until assign-demo-member-roles.sh was run again.
close_reason: Localhost health, one harness chat turn, scheduled-task list, and vault read proven. Chat path is the echo harness because mock-gateway is gone. See notes. Follow-up lp-bhcg.19.

title: Revamp Lanyard onto Cloudflare, starting from localhost
description:
## Why
AWS platform-staging is torn down under OPERATOR HOLD. The product is an always-on agent: personas, tools, cron, memory, files, and a Daytona computer that idles and wakes. Restart that product on localhost, then move the platform services in `deploy/modules/` onto Cloudflare. Daytona stays the computer.

Plan: `docs/plans/0020-cloudflare-platform-revamp/overview.md`.

## Scope
In: localhost proof, backend base URL + API key, D1, R2, Durable Objects, Workers, Daytona wake with the R2 filesystem attached, cron fire, memory, browser use, office on local ONLYOFFICE, program installs on the persistent disk.

Out: re-enabling platform-staging, vendoring agent source, rewriting the portal UI, Workers AI as the model loop, Cloudflare Containers as the agent computer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Child beads land in the order in the plan issue map
- [ ] No terraform apply of platform-staging is part of this epic
- [ ] A localhost chat turn works before any Workers deploy
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Child beads land in the order in the plan issue map
- [ ] No terraform apply of platform-staging is part of this epic
- [ ] A localhost chat turn works before any Workers deploy
notes: Filed 2026-10-15 from a state review. Docker was not available in the filing environment, so the compose stack was not booted.

title: Accept a signed webhook as a trigger that wakes the agent
description:
## Why
Cron and a user message are the triggers that already exist. The next one is an inbound HTTP trigger so something outside the portal can wake the same agent path.

Plan: `docs/plans/0020-cloudflare-platform-revamp/overview.md`. Keyword triggers and Slack stay in plan 0016 and are not this bead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A signed POST creates a turn for one agent
- [ ] The sandbox wakes if it is idle
- [ ] An unsigned or wrong-signature request is rejected
- [ ] The portal shows the trigger source on that turn
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Signed webhook starts a turn and can wake the sandbox
- [ ] Bad signatures are rejected
